audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash and short-term investments as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $2.255 billion, equal to $10.50 per share and 32.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The full cash balance is added in the equity bridge without deducting minimum operating liquidity.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital needs typically increase in the months leading up to the holiday shopping season as we purchase inventory in advance of expected sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably treats 100% of the $2.255 billion balance as distributable. The filing separately reports $279 million of restricted cash in other current assets, so restricted cash is not shown to be included in this bridge amount; the unresolved issue is how much unrestricted cash is nevertheless required for seasonal inventory and operations. The bridge addition is large enough to materially affect every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum unrestricted operating cash using monthly or quarterly cash, inventory, payable and revolver data through several holiday cycles, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A completed Best Buy Health exit contradicts the null perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $27 million disposal cash outflow and $6 million disposal loss filed; post-exit OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A perimeter adjustment could change anchor OE by removing the exited component's earnings, losses and exit cash flows while retaining residual obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: These actions included the exit of a component of our Best Buy Health business that was finalized during the second quarter of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The completed exit and null perimeter create a demonstrated reconciliation gap, but the record does not isolate the exited component's operating earnings or cash requirements. The $101 million Best Buy Health Optimization and China Sourcing initiative is broader than the disposed component and includes impairments and exit costs, so it cannot serve as the perimeter adjustment. The direction and materiality of the recurring post-exit OE change remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a management or ledger-level carve-out of the exited component's revenue, operating costs, capital spending, working capital, disposal effects, exit payments and continuing obligations; recast FY2026 OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Credit-card profit sharing embeds credit-cycle loss exposure in operating owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $459 million of FY2026 revenue, or 136% of the $336.9 million OE anchor; approximately $421 million to $561 million annually across FY2024-FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Credit-card profit sharing enters operating revenue and anchor OE; normalization changes both starting OE and the durability of forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we earn profit-share income and share in any losses from some of our banking partners based on the performance of the programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is demonstrated and large relative to the depressed anchor. FY2026 profit-sharing revenue was approximately 1.2% of $38.278 billion of Domestic revenue. The current percentage lies between FY2025's 1.1% and FY2024's 1.4%, so the supplied record does not demonstrate that FY2026 itself is above a normalized level; normalization could raise or lower OE. Its scale and contractual loss exposure nevertheless make it material to the forecast.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the profit share and any loss allocations into OE for a full credit cycle, obtain contractual loss caps and settlement terms, and rerun the valuation using a cycle-normalized after-tax amount.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain or inconsistently strip recurring optimization costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $190 million of FY2026 restructuring charges, equal to 56.4% of the $336.9 million anchor; approximately $99 million of related restructuring cash payments, equal to 29.4% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained nonrecurring cash costs understate anchor OE, while excluding recurring adaptation costs overstates OE and sustainable margins.
audit_findings.evidence: Restructuring charges in fiscal 2026 were primarily related to a labor and store optimization restructuring initiative that commenced in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and a restructuring initiative focused on optimizing our Best Buy Health business that commenced in the first quarter of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial and successive restructuring activity: $117 million for labor and store optimization plus $101 million for Health optimization and China sourcing, offset by a $28 million reversal from the fiscal-2024 program. What the $336.9 million OE calculation retained or removed is not supplied. Because both the recorded charges and identified cash payments are large relative to the anchor, inconsistent treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing value in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Produce a line-by-line FY2026 OE reconciliation for all $190 million of charges and approximately $99 million of cash payments, classify each as recurring, nonrecurring or perimeter-related, apply the same policy historically, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes an annual earnings anchor with later balance-sheet and share dates without a stub reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: Six-month FY2027 net earnings of $591 million, operating cash flow of $1.296 billion, capital expenditures of $344 million, cash increase of $517 million, dividends and repurchases of $442 million, and 209.728 million filed shares versus 214.74 million valuation shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The date mismatch affects the OE forecast starting point, cash bridge and per-share denominator and can omit or duplicate stub-period economics.
audit_findings.evidence: A large proportion of our revenue and earnings is generated in the fiscal fourth quarter, which includes the majority of the holiday shopping season.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed dates are demonstrated, and the intervening filed activity is large relative to the $336.9 million annual anchor. The August cash balance already reflects six months of earnings, working-capital movements, capital spending and distributions, while the operating forecast remains anchored to January. This does not by itself prove a specific double count, but without an explicit valuation-date convention the net error can run in either direction and is material.
audit_findings.action: Roll January 31 values to September 5 using the six-month statements and subsequent events; reconcile interim OE, the $517 million cash increase, $442 million of distributions, debt and the September 2 share count exactly once, then rerun from a consistent valuation date.

audit_findings.title: Vendor-allowance estimation is material relative to the depressed anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $45 million filed net-earnings sensitivity, equal to 13.4% of anchor OE; approximately $632 million or $2.94 per share under base-case DCF scaling
audit_findings.mechanism: Allowance recognition changes cost of sales and anchor OE; a persistent adjustment scales projected OE and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: A 10% change in our vendor funding deferral as of January 31, 2026, would have affected net earnings by approximately $45 million in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The $45 million sensitivity is not evidence that an error occurred: the filing says the deferral was relatively stable, and the auditor tested vendor allowances as a critical audit matter. It nevertheless establishes material scale against the depressed anchor. If a $45 million difference persisted through the base forecast, the model's $4.733 billion operating value on $336.9 million of OE implies an approximately $632 million, or $2.94-per-share, value effect. Acceleration would overstate value and deferral would understate it.
audit_findings.action: Tie recognized and deferred allowances to contracts, sell-through, inventory and subsequent cash settlement; determine whether FY2026 contains an unusual timing difference and rerun only the supported normalized adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $20.3 million FY2025 residual; an equal-amount anchor adjustment would imply about $285 million or $1.33 per share in the base case
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic expense would be added to OE, increasing operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2025 $845.0m (97.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value. The residual is 2.4% of the supplied $845 million FY2025 composite D&A, or approximately $20.3 million. As a scale comparison, applying an equal amount to the anchor and the base case's implied 14.05-times operating-value multiple would add about $1.33 per share, only 4.1% of the $32.54 base value and insufficient to alter the valuation conclusion relative to the $90.27 market price. The actual FY2026 effect is not established.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset disclosures; rerun only if evidence identifies an eligible add-back, using the amount applicable to the FY2026 anchor rather than the FY2025 proxy.
